How it works

1

Install ThetaDesk and sign in with Google, so your setup is backed up from the first minute.

2

Connect your broker: the app shows each broker's own steps to create a free API key.

3

Practise with paper money. For live orders, add a static IP registered with your broker — the guide shows how.

Why a static IP? Since 1 April 2026, SEBI's rules for retail algorithmic trading require orders placed through your own API key to come from a fixed internet address registered with your broker (one main and one backup; family members may share). Prices, charts and paper trading work without one.

Questions

Does ThetaDesk hold my money or place trades for me?

No. ThetaDesk is software you run on your own PC or phone. It trades only in your own broker account, through your broker's official API, and in "confirm" mode it waits for your approval on every order. Your money stays with your broker.

Where are my broker keys kept?

Encrypted on your device. If you sign in with Google, an encrypted backup is kept so a new phone or PC can restore your setup with one sign-in.

Can I use it on my phone and my PC?

Yes. Your accounts, settings and closed trades sync through your Google sign-in. One device trades at a time: tap "Use my accounts here" to switch. That stops two logins from logging each other out of your broker.

What does it cost?

ThetaDesk is free during early access. You need your own broker account (API access for orders is free at most brokers) and, for live orders, a static IP.

Is this investment advice?

No. ThetaDesk's market readings and suggestions are rules applied to market data, not advice. Trading in futures and options can lose you more than you expect; you are responsible for every order you place or approve.
